item.title: Trump administration to dig at triumphal arch site despite no final federal approvals
item.description: The Trump administration says it will break ground on a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., without final federal approval and despite an ongoing lawsuit.
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration says it will break ground on a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., without final federal approval and despite an ongoing lawsuit.

item.title: Week in Politics: Trump's face on the coin; reshaping the capital; the midterms
item.description: President Trump is the first living president to have his face on a coin. He's also reshaping Washington in his image, and working to influence midterm elections.
item.content:encoded: President Trump is the first living president to have his face on a coin. He's also reshaping Washington in his image, and working to influence midterm elections.

item.title: Voters are fed up with data centers. Both parties are trying to cash in for midterms
item.description: Democrats and Republicans have found common ground in this campaign season. Both parties have poured millions into ads attacking data centers as the public continues to protest the AI facilities.

item.title: Flock cameras draw opposition from across the political spectrum
item.description: As political races heat up heading into the midterms, candidates from both parties are increasingly joining the fray to voice concerns over Flock surveillance cameras.

item.title: 4 things investigators learned about the dysfunction at Trump's Labor Department
item.description: A report from Labor Department investigators found former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer violated her own department's policy prohibiting harassment. She resigned in April.

item.title: 'Hidden tribunals': Immigration court due process in tumult with new locations
item.description: The new effort appears to be another tactic in a broader Trump administration strategy to short-circuit immigrants' already limited due process options in order to speed deportations.

item.title: El-Sayed split Michigan Democrats. Whether they unify could decide Senate control
item.description: After a bruising Senate primary, Michigan Democrats are trying to unify to hold onto a must-win seat. But healing those fissures is proving not so simple.

item.title: Trump's arch may break ground without final approval. Veterans are trying to stop it
item.description: Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says "excavation work" will begin in the next two weeks, without approval from a key federal body. Veterans who sued over the arch want a judge to intervene before then.

item.description: The Trump administration wants to end tax-exempt status for universities with certain race-based programs. Wesleyan President Michael Roth says the plan could frighten schools.

item.title: The Trump administration still aims to make state citizenship lists ahead of midterms
item.description: The Trump administration is taking the unprecedented step of creating lists of adult citizens who are eligible to vote in each state – but will not meet its own deadline 60 days before Election Day.
